transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because... well, I just can't stop feeling like I'm a danger and a disappointment. I work as a nurse, and I had this one near-miss recently. Ever since then, I just feel like it proves I'm not meant to be a nurse at all. It's just... I keep thinking everyone would be better off without me.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or activities?

Yeah, I have. I used to clear my head by doing things like jogging, knitting, cooking, or reading after my classes. But now... I just come home and sit on my bed in my scrubs. I just can't seem to make myself care about any of it anymore.
Do you find yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual, even when it's not entirely your fault?

Yeah, all the time. Like I mentioned when I first sat down, that's really the main reason I'm here. I just feel like a constant disappointment. That near-miss at work... I just can't let it go, and I blame myself completely for it. It makes me feel like I'm an actual danger to my patients, and it just proves I shouldn't be a nurse at all. I just keep having that same thought, that everyone would just be better off without me around to mess things up.
Have you had thoughts about hurting yourself or ending your life, even if you don't have a specific plan in mind?

I don't have a plan to actually hurt myself, no. But... I do keep having these thoughts. Like it would just be easier if I didn't wake up in the morning. Or if I could just disappear somehow. That way I wouldn't be around to mess anything else up again.
Have you noticed that you feel more tired or have less energy than usual, even when you haven't done anything physically or mentally draining?

Not really, no. I mean, my shifts at the hospital are pretty exhausting, so I'm usually tired after work anyway. But on my days off... I don't think my actual energy levels are any lower than they used to be. Like I said, I just sit on my bed because I don't care to do anything else, not because I'm too physically drained to move. So, no, I haven't really noticed feeling more tired than usual.
Have you been having trouble sleeping, like difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up earlier than you intend to?

Yeah, I have. At night, I just lie there in bed replaying patient charts and medication calculations in my head, so it takes a long time to actually drift off. And then when I finally do fall asleep, I always seem to wake up way before my alarm goes off. I wake up already exhausted, and just... immediately scared that I missed something important. So, yeah, my sleep really hasn't been great.
Would you say that you feel depressed most of the day, nearly every day, not just in response to specific stressors like the near-miss at work?

Yeah, I would say so. It's definitely not just about work. Most days, I just... I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling right in my chest, and it doesn't really go away. Even when I'm at the clinic, you know, smiling at my patients in Spanish and trying to act normal... I feel like I'm just barely holding myself together. So, yeah, it's pretty much all day, every day.
Have you found it difficult to focus on tasks, follow conversations, or make decisions lately, even simple ones like what to wear or what to eat?

Yeah, I definitely have. It's been pretty frustrating, honestly. Like, I'll find myself having to read the same medication order or... or a lecture slide for school over and over again because my brain just feels completely foggy. None of it seems to stick. And making decisions is hard, too. Even just small choices, like trying to figure out what to chart first at work, can just totally freeze me up.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about things most days, even when there isn’t a clear reason for it?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about work and school, like making a mistake or falling behind... but I wouldn't say I just feel anxious for no reason. It's more of that heavy, sad feeling I mentioned than just being worried all the time.
Have you noticed that you’ve been moving more slowly than usual, or that you can’t sit still and feel restless?

Yeah, I've noticed I'm moving slower. People at the clinic have actually asked if I'm tired because I'm just... slower when I'm getting supplies or moving around the rooms. And sometimes, even when someone asks me a simple question, it feels like it takes me a few extra seconds just to process it and get the words out to answer them. I don't really feel restless or anything, just... slow.
Have your feelings of sadness, guilt, and difficulty concentrating been affecting your ability to function at work or in your daily life?

Yes, it really has been affecting things. I've actually fallen behind in my nursing prerequisites because I just can't focus. And at the clinic... I've had to ask my coworkers to double-check things for me, tasks I used to do with no problem. It's gotten to the point where I'm just afraid to take on my normal responsibilities because I don't trust myself right now.
How long have you been feeling this way — the sadness, guilt, and difficulty concentrating — has it been going on for at least two weeks, or is it something that’s gotten worse recently?

It's definitely been longer than two weeks. I'd say it's been going on for about a year and two months now. It really started right after I graduated high school, when I jumped straight into taking college classes and working full-time at the clinic. It's just been a constant thing since then.
Have your feelings of sadness, guilt, and difficulty concentrating been present nearly every day for the entire two-week period or longer, without significant variation in severity?

Yeah, it's pretty much every day. I mean... I haven't really kept track of whether it gets better or worse on certain days, to be honest. It just feels like it's always there in the background, so I don't think it changes all that much. It's just kind of a constant weight.
